title: 5G SALE Act
official_summary:
5G Spectrum Authority Licensing Enforcement Act or the 5G SALE Act

This act temporarily authorizes the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to process applications for licenses or permits for the use of specified bands of the electromagnetic spectrum that were auctioned on or before March 9, 2023. The authorization terminates 90 days after the enactment of the act.

The FCC has not processed the licenses or permits for the previously auctioned spectrum because its authority to conduct auctions lapsed on March 9, 2023.

summary.headline: Temporarily lets the FCC finish issuing licenses for wireless airwaves it auctioned before its auction authority expired in March 2023.
summary.what_it_does: The FCC's legal authority to hold spectrum auctions expired on March 9, 2023. Because of this, the FCC had not issued licenses for airwaves that companies had already won in auctions held before that date. This law gives the FCC temporary power to process those license applications. That power ends 90 days after the law was enacted.

who_it_affects.group: Companies that won FCC spectrum auctions on or before March 9, 2023
who_it_affects.how: The FCC can now process their pending license applications so they can use the airwaves they bid on.
The agency gets a 90-day window to process applications for these previously auctioned airwaves.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: December 19, 2023; the authority expires 90 days later (about March 18, 2024).
